name: skills
description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
one_liner: A free, public collection of one engineer's day-to-day coding habits (how to plan, document, and review work) packaged so an AI coding assistant can follow them automatically.
buyer: An engineering manager at a small-to-mid startup who wants every AI coding assistant on the team to work the same way, without writing a playbook from scratch.
business_use_cases: A startup's engineering lead installs it so every engineer's AI assistant follows the same intake process (spec first, then plan, then code), cutting rework from misread requests.
A solo SaaS founder uses the glossary skill to teach their AI assistant project-specific jargon, so its first drafts need fewer corrections.
A dev-tooling consultant forks it as the starter kit they hand every new client, charging for the setup and tailoring.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid onboarding calls that customize the skill set (glossary, workflow) to a specific company's codebase.

steal_this: This weekend, strip it down to 3 core skills and offer a paid one-hour 'AI workflow setup' call for small dev teams who don't want to read the whole repo themselves.
